Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility · School & learning

department noun

a section of an organization, with its own work

also departments, university department, government department, that’s not my department

classical

Ter. Ph. 72–73: prōvinciam cēpistī dūram
Plaut. Cas. 103: tuam in prōvinciam

prōvincia, prōvinciae f.

noun, first declension

a charge, someone’s department: the work assigned to them

Properly the task assigned to a magistrate; in comedy any job in someone’s charge, as in “that’s not my department”.

Examples

  • ō Geta, prōvinciam cēpistī dūram

    oh, Geta, that’s a hard job you’ve taken onTer. Ph. 72–73

  • quīn rūrī es in praefectūrā tuā? quīn potius quod lēgātum est tibi negōtium, id cūrās atque urbānīs rēbus tē apstinēs?

    why aren’t you in the country at your own post? Why don’t you see to the business you were given, and keep out of town affairs?Plaut. Cas. 99–101

Other words

  • officium, officiī n. — the staff of an office; an administrative department

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Dig. 1.18.6; Treb. Poll. Gall. 17.8: officia palātīna (Lewis & Short)

    Classically a duty or a service.

  • facultās, facultātis f. — a faculty or department of a university

    noun, third declension · also used · medieval · Traupman 302: litterārum classicārum facultās, department of classics; M-O s.v. department: major division of university

    Classically ability, means.

  • ministerium, ministeriī n. — a government department, a ministry

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. minister: ministry, (governmental) department

    Classically an office or a service (Lewis & Short).

See also job, manager, office, university, department store.
